question: Acid catalysed dehydration of t-butanol is faster than that of n-butanol. This is because
option1: The three electron-donating methyl groups in t-butanol increase the electron density on the oxygen atom, making it significantly more basic than n-butanol. This facilitates rapid protonation by the acid catalyst, which is the rate-determining step.
option2: The bulky tert-butyl group causes severe steric crowding around the carbinol carbon. This steric acceleration weakens the C–O bond, allowing water to leave more easily, whereas the linear n-butyl chain experiences no such steric relief.
option3: The three electron-donating methyl groups in t-butanol increase the electron density on the oxygen atom, making it significantly more basic than n-butanol. This facilitates rapid protonation by the acid catalyst, which is the rate-determining step.
option4: t-Butanol dehydrates to form isobutylene, a highly substituted and thermodynamically stable alkene. This large thermodynamic driving force lowers the overall energy of the system, thereby increasing the rate of the reaction compared to the less stable 1-butene formed from n-butanol.
